title: Si Bien: Granting a Point Formally

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de que* and *pese a* "despite" from B1 Unit 32 (*A pesar de que era caro, lo compramos*), *sin embargo* and *no obstante* from B1 Unit 1, and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. Another way to grant a point is *si bien* "although it is true that". It is formal: you find it in reports, essays, speeches and news. It takes the indicative, because the speaker confirms that the fact is true and then gives the point that matters more.

sections.title: Five ways to grant a point
rows: Aunque el plan es caro, tiene ventajas.
Everyday: although the plan is expensive, it has advantages.
A pesar de que el plan es caro, tiene ventajas.
Despite the fact that the plan is expensive... (You know it from B1 Unit 32.)
Pese al precio, el plan tiene ventajas.
Despite the price... (*Pese a* + noun, B1 Unit 32.)
Si bien el plan es caro, tiene ventajas.
Formal: although it is true that the plan is expensive, it has advantages.
El plan es caro; no obstante, tiene ventajas.
The plan is expensive; nevertheless, it has advantages.

sections.title: Using si bien
sections.content: The *si bien* clause grants a true point, and the main clause says what you really want to say. It often opens the sentence (*Si bien el plan es caro, tiene ventajas*), but it can also sit in the middle between commas (*El plan, si bien es caro, tiene ventajas*). The verb after *si bien* is in the indicative in this lesson. It is two words, so do not confuse it with *sí* "yes" or with *si* "if", and do not add *que* after it.

items.spanish: Si bien el proyecto es caro, ofrece muchas ventajas.
items.english: Although the project is expensive, it offers many advantages.

items.spanish: Si bien llegamos tarde, pudimos ver el final del concierto.
items.english: Although we arrived late, we were able to see the end of the concert.

items.spanish: Esta ciudad, si bien es pequeña, tiene mucha vida cultural.
items.english: This city, although it is small, has a lot of cultural life.

items.spanish: Si bien tiene poca experiencia, trabaja con mucho empeño.
items.english: Although he has little experience, he works with great determination.

sections.content: Choose by register. With friends or in a message, say *aunque*. In a report, a speech or an essay, *si bien* sounds right. Both take the indicative for a fact, but only *aunque* also has the subjunctive for a possibility, so for "even if" you need *aunque*, not *si bien*.
